title: In Vitro Wound Healing Assay to Evaluate Cell Migration

Después de observar la monocapa celular en cada uno de los pozos y sin retirar el medio, realizar la herida o ruptura in vitro pasando con una punta estéril de 200 µL sobre la mitad del pozo en direccion vertical y perpendicular a las señas realizadas en el reverso del pozo. Utilizar 1 punta nueva por cada pozo. Retirar el medio y lavar tres veces con PBS 1X (NaCl 0.14M; KCl 2,7mM; Na2HPO4 10.1mM; KH2PO4 1.8mM pH 7.4). Adicionar 300 µL de fibronectina a una concentración final de 5µg/mL e incubar por 1 hora a 37°C y 5% de CO 2 . Lavar tres veces con PBS 1X. Añadir los controles como sigue (1mL/pozo): Blanco (B) : medio de cultivo (DMEM 1X al 2% de SFB) Control positivo (CP) :para células HaCat: Factor de Crecimiento Epidérmico (EGF) (stock 50 µg/mL) concentración final en el pozo de 40 ng/mL. Control negativo (CN): hidrocortisona concentración final de 10µg/mL. Tratamientos (T#): evaluar en medio de cultivo (DMEM 1X al 2% de SFB) para un volumen final de 1 mL/pozo. Proceda a incubar por las horas correspondientes a 37°C y 5% de CO 2 y tome las fotos correspondientes. Tabla. steps.title: Mark wells with scalpel
steps.instruction: Use a scalpel or bisturí to make two horizontal scratches 5 mm apart on the reverse side of each well of a 24‑well plate as positional markers.

steps.title: Prepare and seed cells
steps.instruction: Detach cells with Trypsin‑EDTA (Gibco 25200056) until they are individually suspended and viability is >90 %; count cells and seed 250 000 cells per well in a 24‑well plate containing DMEM 1X supplemented with 2 % fetal bovine serum, 1 X antibiotic‑antimycotic, and 1 mM sodium pyruvate; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 6–8 h to reach 85–90 % confluence; use cells that are 2–3 passages after thawing.

substeps.instruction: Detach cells with Trypsin‑EDTA (Gibco 25200056) ensuring >90 % viability.
Count cells and calculate volume needed for 250 000 cells per well.
Add cells to each well of a 24‑well plate containing DMEM 1X + 2 % FBS, 1 X antibiotic‑antimycotic, 1 mM sodium pyruvate.
Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 6–8 h until 85–90 % confluence is reached.

steps.title: Create wound (scratch)
steps.instruction: Using the scalpel, create a linear scratch across the cell monolayer in each well, aligning the scratch with the previously placed markers to ensure consistent position and width.

steps.title: Capture images at defined times
steps.instruction: At 0, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h, acquire four 40× inverted‑microscope images per well. Image order: positive control, negative control, sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4, vehicle, medium. Place the X‑marker at the centre of the field to locate the same region, avoid having the marker within the visual field, keep illumination, contrast and diffuser position constant, label each image with its time point and well identifier, and store images in separate time‑point folders and a spreadsheet.

substeps.instruction: Set microscope to 40× objective and adjust illumination, contrast, and diffuser.
Locate the X‑marker (or the scar) at the centre of the field; ensure the marker itself is not visible in the image.
Capture four images per well in the specified order.
Save each image with a filename indicating time point, well, and treatment; record the filename in a spreadsheet and place the file in the folder for that time point.

steps.title: Measure wound area with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open each image in ImageJ and run the macro file MigracionCelularIndividual.ijm (Plugins > Macros > Run) to obtain the wound area. If the macro does not detect the wound correctly, use the Freehand selection tool to trace the wound border without releasing the mouse button, then press Ctrl + M to display the measured area.

substeps.instruction: Select Plugins > Macros > Run and choose MigracionCelularIndividual.ijm; the macro will output the wound area.
If the macro fails, select Freehand selection, draw the wound contour while keeping the mouse button pressed, release to close the selection, then press Ctrl + M to view the area measurement.

steps.title: Calculate wound‑closure percentage
steps.instruction: For each well compute % closure = ((initial area – area at time X) / initial area) × 100; obtain four measurements per well (triplicate), giving 12 values per treatment per time point.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Test normality of each treatment group with the D’Agostino‑Pearson test (α = 0.05). If data are normal, run a two‑way ANOVA in GraphPad Prism, then compare each treatment to the medium control using Student’s t‑test; consider differences significant when P < 0.05.
